subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks for taking the time earlier — great discussion. Per our call, here’s a concise recap of the technical requirements, pain points, and agreed next steps so we stay aligned. I’ve included Rishi and Vivek from our engineering team on the thread for any follow-ups.

Summary of pain points / goals (what you told us):
- P1: Sub-100ms 90th percentile latency for 512-token generation on customer-facing chat flows (peak traffic is expected at 200 TPS for peak product launches).
- P2: Consistent throughput to support sustained batch inference for nightly offline scoring (target 100k docs/day) without affecting realtime SLA.
- P3: Data residency & audit log requirements (EU customers must have logs retained in-region for 1 year; currently storing logs in central US datacenter causes compliance workarounds).

Model & workload requirements:
- Model family: mix of 7B and 13B decoder-only models (open LLM variants); occasional fallback to larger 33B model for complex queries.
- Typical sequence length: 256 tokens in prompts, 512 tokens including generation on realtime flows.
- KV-cache reuse expected for conversational sessions (session length up to ~30 turns).

Deployment topology preferences discussed:
- Primary: Dedicated capacity (GPU pool) in us-west-2 for realtime endpoints to hit latency SLOs.
- Secondary: Private regionally isolated deployment (EU) for regulated European customers to meet data residency rules.
- Autoscale policy: predictable reserved capacity for baseline, burst to shared capacity for spikes (we discussed Redwood Dedicated + burst).

Initial SLO targets (agreed as workshop baselines):
- Realtime: 90th percentile <= 100ms for 512-token response on 13B model at baseline 50 TPS; degrade gracefully under burst to 200 TPS with fallback to 7B variant.
- Throughput: sustained offline batch processing of 100k docs/day with 24-hour SLAs for completion.
- Availability: 99.9% uptime for realtime endpoints with multi-AZ failover.

Action items / next steps:
1) Rishi to draft an initial topology diagram recommendation (GPU SKUs, expected shard counts, autoscale knobs) — ETA: Tue, Jun 29.
2) Marissa to share draft TCO and rough monthly cost estimates for the baseline and burst scenarios — ETA: Mon, Jul 5.
3) Alex/Priya to validate compliance constraints (data residency list + audit log retention specifics) and share any required controls — ETA: Wed, Jun 30.
4) Align on a follow-up deep-dive next week to finalize model sizing and canary rollout plan.

Attachments: redwood_slo_design.pdf (design + preliminary sizing), acme_kpi_matrix.xlsx (your KPI mapping from the call).

Please reply with any corrections to the capture above. If that looks right, we’ll schedule a follow-up deep-dive with infra leads (Rishi) and your platform engineer.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting a pilot configured.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifications and responses inline: 

- Latency: the 100ms 90p is for customer-facing chat flows only. For internal agent-assist flows we can tolerate up to ~250ms. We’ll confirm exact traffic split in the follow-up.
- Throughput: the 100k docs/day is an estimate for batch enrichment. We may push to 200k in Q4; plan should be elastic.
- Models: correct on 7B/13B primary, but note that for certain enterprise customers we need a 33B option pinned behind an auth gate. Fallback strategy is fine.

Compliance notes (from Priya):
- EU data residency requirement: logs and payloads for EU customers must be retained and stored in eu-central-1 and not be replicated to other regions for at least 12 months.
- We also need SOC2 + annual attestation for access controls documented before pilot kickoff.

Action updates:
- I’ll send a consolidated list of the EU customer IDs and their required retention windows by Tue.
- Can we get an initial run-rate estimate for the baseline (50 TPS) vs. peak (200 TPS) including both hosted and dedicated pricing? That will help our procurement.

Also looping in Priya for the compliance confirmations — Priya, feel free to add anything I missed.

Alex

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology

Alex — quick technical follow-up and proposed next steps from our infra side. I’ve sketched a recommended topology and sizing in the attached PDF. High-level notes: 

- GPU SKUs: For 13B at sub-100ms 90p with 512 tokens we recommend A100/80GB-class or equivalent multi-instance setup with model sharding and KV-cache co-location. For cost-optimized realtime at 7B, an H100/80GB or equivalent quantized pipeline can be used.
- Shard counts: baseline pool: 6-8 model replicas for 13B to support 50 TPS with headroom; plan autoscale to 18 replicas for burst to 200 TPS with pre-warmed pools for hot paths.
- Canary plan: 10% traffic canary to a lightweight quantized 7B variant to validate latency, then expand with A/B routing.
- Region strategy: deploy dedicated realtime in us-west-2 for US customers; deploy private EU control plane with EU compute (eu-central-1) for regulated customers. We’ll ensure audit logs are retained per your policy (1 year).
- Audit/SOC2: we can provide SOC2 report and our access-control runbooks; operations will need a short questionnaire filled out by your compliance team.

Next steps I’ll own:
- Share a topology diagram + sizing table (attached) and a short TCO for baseline vs peak by Mon, Jul 5.
- Draft canary rollout checklist and monitoring hooks (latency percentiles, token-level cost, KV hit rates) for review by Tue, Jun 29.

If you’re available next Wed 30th or Thu 1st for a 60-minute deep-dive, I can walk through the diagram and we can finalize the autoscale policy.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
